jobs.description: Nunez Community College Employment Opportunities The state constitution defines the “state civil service” as everyone employed by a state agency or by a joint state/federal or state/local agency, “regardless of the source of funds used to pay for such employment.” The only exception is commissioned State Police officers, who are in a separate civil service system. The constitution divides the state civil service into “classified” and “unclassified” employees and states that “Persons not included in the unclassified service are in the classified service.” The constitution designates certain specific categories of employees as unclassified and gives the State Civil Service Commission the authority to designate other positions as unclassified as it deems appropriate. Please select the menu item below to view the position classification that you are interested in: Classified Employment Opportunities Classified positions and the employees who serve in them are subject to the provisions of the Civil Service Rules. Candidates must have an MD or DO degree (or equivalent), hold a Louisiana medical license prior to start date, and the following: • Dual boarded/eligible (or equivalent) in Pediatric Critical Care Medicine AND Pediatric Cardiology; OR Board certified/eligible (or equivalent) in Pediatric Critical Care Medicine with significant cardiac critical care experience; OR board certified/eligible (or equivalent) in Pediatric Cardiology with formal advanced training in Cardiac Intensive Care Medicine (minimum of 12 months)This is a full-time faculty position at the Assistant, Associate Professor, or Professor level (non-tenure, clinical track) with academic rank to be determined by the candidate’s credentials and experience. Clinical service time will be commensurate with the needs of the Division and intensive care unit and includes in-house night coverage. The position also entails a commitment to the teaching of physician trainees at all levels (including medical students), advanced practice providers, nurses, and other unit-based staff. Faculty members are also expected to participate in various university and hospital-driven training and educational activities, including quality improvement and care process improvement initiatives, and are strongly encouraged to pursue basic science or clinical research interests, which will require separate efforts to obtain outside grant funding wherever possible. Currently, approximately 200 heart catheterizations (75% interventional) and close to 250 cardiothoracic surgeries are performed each year at Manning Family Children’s, a 247-bed tertiary care teaching complex located in the heart of New Orleans which serves the entire State of Louisiana and the central Gulf Coast region. The CICU is staffed 24/7 with 5 cardiac intensivists and we are actively recruiting 3 more intensivists. The Heart Center participates in STS, PC4, Impact, NPC-QIC, ACTION, and other major registries.The Heart Center has an ACGME-accredited LSUHSC pediatric cardiology fellowship training program. There are excellent opportunities for clinical, translational and basic research, particularly with the LSUHSC Cardiovascular Center of Excellence as well as the Heart Center’s Research Core. The successful candidate is expected to have strong clinical skills, have an interest in research, and participate actively in the teaching of residents and fellows. jobs.description: ASSISTANT PROFESSOR / ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR / PROFESSOR, CLINICAL - PEDIATRIC CARDIOLOGIST - ADULT CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE New Orleans, Louisiana, United States Faculty Medicine View favorites Title: ASSISTANT PROFESSOR / ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR / PROFESSOR, CLINICAL - PEDIATRIC CARDIOLOGIST - ADULT CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE Employee Type: Faculty Department: Pediatrics Campus Location: CHILDRENS Job Summary/Basic Functions The Division of Pediatric Cardiology and the Department of Pediatrics at the Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center and the Heart Center of Manning Family Children’s is seeking a Cardiologist with expertise in adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) to join its growing ACHD program. The applicant should have specific expertise in adult congenital heart disease and be board certified/eligible in ACHD. The ACHD program recently obtained accreditation and is the only accredited program in the state of Louisiana. The candidate would be expected to grow this expanding program by performing clinical ACHD duties in both the outpatient and inpatient settings. Manning Family Children’s is the founding member of a 6-hospital health system titled LCMC (Louisiana Children’s Medical Center). Extensive relationships exist between Manning Family Children’s and all other partner hospitals in the LCMC group, especially Touro Infirmary, University Medical Center and East Jefferson General Hospital. Additional opportunities exist in pulmonary hypertension, exercise physiology, our Fontan clinic, coronary artery disease/anomalies, imaging and other Heart Center programs depending on the candidate’s expertise and interest. Academic appointment will be at the rank of Assistant, Associate or Full Professor. A joint appointment between Pediatric and Adult Cardiology is also possible. Other Information About the Position The Heart Center Faculty includes a team of 19 physicians, two cardiac surgeons, and 4 cardiac anesthesiologists. Subspeciality care in the Heart Center includes non-invasive imaging, interventional cardiology, electrophysiology, expertise in Fontan management, home-monitoring, neurodevelopment, pulmonary hypertension, pediatric coronary artery disease, and heart failure. Currently, more than 200 heart catheterizations (75% interventional), close to 250 cardiothoracic surgeries, and 11,000 ambulatory visits are performed each year at Manning Family Children’s. Manning Family Children’s Hospital is the only freestanding children’s hospital in Louisiana and serves as the primary pediatric teaching site for LSUHSC Pediatrics. Manning Family Children’s is a 263-bed, not-for-profit pediatric medical center offering a comprehensive range of services for children from birth to 21 years, with more than 600 pediatric providers and 3,000 employees solely dedicated to the care of kids. With an unwavering commitment to child health, we have proudly served as the Gulf South’s only comprehensive children’s hospital for 70 years – transforming countless lives since we first opened our doors in 1955. The hospital is home to a growing array of pediatric subspecialists and houses state-of-the-art facilities.Hospital leadership is committed to programmatic growth and excellence. jobs.description: T hank you for your interest in employment with Louisiana Tech University. The College of Engineering and Science (COES) at Louisiana Tech University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position in the Computer Science program. We seek highly qualified, research-active scholars specializing in cybersecurity and cyber operations. Candidates with expertise combining cybersecurity with artificial intelligence, machine learning, quantum computing, robotics, smart health, the Internet of Things (IoT), and cyber-physical systems are encouraged to apply. Louisiana Tech University, recognized as a national university by the 2024 U.S. News & World Report, is designated as a Center of Academic Excellence in Cybersecurity for Cyber Defense (CAE-CD) and Cyber Research (CAE-R). The College of Engineering and Science is deeply committed to advancing cybersecurity research and education, addressing critical challenges such as cyber resilience, critical infrastructure protection, and emerging cyber threats. Faculty research efforts are supported by specialized research centers, including the Cybersecurity Applied Innovation Laboratory ( CyAIL ) and the Center for Secure Cyberspace (CSC), which facilitate collaborative research and provide opportunities for securing external research funding. The College is experiencing significant growth, with nearly 3,000 students, including approximately 1 3 0 doctoral students among 300 graduate students . Annual research expenditures within the College have averaged $16 million over the past five years. The Computer Science program serves approximately 550 undergraduate majors and is the second-largest degree granting program at the university. jobs.description: T hank you for your interest in employment with Louisiana Tech University. In support of its recently announced $80M+ partnership with private industry and state entities to support microelectronics manufacturing and research (https://www.latech.edu/news/louisiana-tech-radiance-technologies-and-led-partner-to-construct-new-microchip-facility-in-ruston.php), the College of Engineering and Science at Louisiana Tech University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position to support the research and educational mission of its Institute for Micromanufacturing (IfM) research center. Candidates of particular interest include those with demonstrated research accomplishments in the fields of microelectronics, microelectronics packaging, microelectronics failure, semiconductor materials, solid state/quantum devices, zero-trust processing architectures, and/or photonics. Candidates must hold a doctorate or equivalent degree in an engineering or science field relevant the application spaces listed above, and must be viable to obtain a security clearance for defense-related funding opportunities with our strategic partners. Successful tenure-track candidates are expected to actively participate in multidisciplinary research efforts in the College; initiate, build and sustain an externally funded research program; and supervise masters and doctoral students. Excellent written and oral communication skills, strong teaching skills, and a commitment to high quality university and professional service are also expected. The College is especially interested in qualified candidates who can contribute, through their research, teaching and/or service, to the diversity and excellence of the academic community. To build a diverse workforce the college encourages applications from women, minorities, veterans, and individuals with disabilities. See the College website for more information (http://coes.latech.edu). Along with your application, compile a single PDF that includes 1) cover letter; 2) curriculum vitae; 3) statement of research interests and plans; 4) description of teaching experience and interests; and 5) the names and contact information for at least three references. Louisiana Tech University’s Institute for Micromanufacturing (IfM) is one of only a small number of EPSCoR state R&D facilities committed to research, education, and training in semiconductor materials and microfabrication. Housed in its own dedicated facility built in 1995 with the help of federal and State investments, the IfM plays an indispensable role in supporting basic and applied research as well as workforce development both in the region and nationally. Students trained at IfM occupy R&D and management positions at Intel, AMD, Samsung, SONY, Texas Instruments, Meta, and other companies that make use of semiconductor and microscale processing technologies, as well as at several Defense-serving companies such as Raytheon, Northrup Grumman, Boeing, and Radiance Technologies. The IfM offers over 20,000 sq. ft. of research space including 5,000 sq. ft. of cleanrooms for the design, fabrication, and testing of application-specific microsystems and the basic science behind them. In addition to scientific research, the IfM also includes in its mission the education and training to the next generation of scientists and engineers. More information on the IfM research center can be found at its website (http://ifm.latech.edu). jobs.description: T hank you for your interest in employment with Louisiana Tech University. The School of Biological Sciences offers undergraduate degrees in Biology, Environmental Science, Medical Laboratory Science, and Nutrition and Dietetics as well as MS degrees in Biology, Molecular Sciences and Nanotechnology (MSNT), and Nutrition and Dietetics, and a PhD degree in MSNT. In total, the School has ~650 undergraduate students and ~20-25 graduate students. The School of Biological Sciences at Louisiana Tech University invites applications for a full-time, 12-month Facilities Coordinator/Instructor position. The appointment is approximately 50% instruction and 50% service, with instructional responsibilities typically including five undergraduate biology courses annually, including summer instruction. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Instruction : Teach undergraduate biology lecture and laboratory courses as assigned, appropriate to the Instructor's area of expertise. Maintain inventories of laboratory equipment, instructional supplies, and other School assets. Perform other duties assigned by the Director of the School of Biological Sciences. Minimum Qualifications Master's degree in Biology or a closely related discipline from an accredited institution. Demonstrated ability to teach undergraduate biology lecture and laboratory courses. Experience supporting laboratory operations and maintaining scientific equipment. Ability to maintain and troubleshoot laboratory equipment and support instructional facilities. Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills. Valid driver's license or ability to obtain one consistent with University requirements. Preferred Qualifications College-level teaching experience in biology. Experience maintaining laboratory equipment and coordinating laboratory operations. Experience managing laboratory inventories, supplies, and equipment procurement. Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with a variety of audiences, including students, faculty, staff, and the public. About Louisiana Tech University: Louisiana Tech University is a vibrant and inclusive community dedicated to excellence in education, research, and service. This role focuses on building students' confidence and competence in verbal and nonverbal communication, critical listening, and audience-centered speech development. Duties and Responsibilities: I. Teaching ● Provide learning experiences in accordance with students' needs and abilities ● Create a learning environment in which all students are treated equitably ● Make adequate preparation for the instructional process to ensure that course content is presented in a manner suitable for students with varying learning styles ● Direct students not on the official class roster to the Office of Enrollment Management to correct enrollment problems, restricting attendance to officially enrolled students ● Meet all scheduled classes within the appropriate timeframe and provide opportunities for student conferences either online, by phone, or through face-to-face interactions ● Be punctual with respect to class meetings and provide instruction for the entire class period ● Notify academic program manager/department chair of absences and promptly provide course continuity plans ● Utilize Canvas or other learning management systems as appropriate and required ● Use instructional and technological resources such as the library, Digital Learning and Academic Support Center (DLASC), and computer technology as appropriate ● Provide classroom instruction in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 and federal harassment policies ● Alert the department chair or academic program manager of any instances of academic dishonesty ● Maintain a minimum of 10 office hours per week ● Maintain accurate grade and attendance records ● Assess learning outcomes and utilize results when planning and preparing future courses ● Administer final examinations for students during the scheduled exam period ● Participate in assigning course credit via prior learning assessment ● Participate in the teaching evaluation process II. jobs.college: Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center-New Orleans
jobs.description: INSTRUCTOR / ASSISTANT PROFESSOR / ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR / PROFESSOR - CLINICAL, FAMILY MEDICINE 497597 Lake Charles, Louisiana, United States Faculty Medicine Title: INSTRUCTOR / ASSISTANT PROFESSOR / ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR / PROFESSOR - CLINICAL, FAMILY MEDICINE Employee Type: Faculty Department: Family Medicine Campus Location: FM-LAKE CHARLES RESIDENTS Job Summary/Basic Functions The Department of Family Medicine of the LSU Health Sciences Center – New Orleans is seeking applications for an academic faculty position to serve as a Behavioral Health Specialist/Educator. This position is based in Lake Charles. Appointment will be at the rank of Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor (non-tenure, clinical track), dependent on qualifications. Incumbent will be a vital member of the Family Medicine Residency Program, providing expertise in the integration of behavioral health principles and practices within the primary care setting. The Behavioral Health Specialist/Educator will share responsibilities with the Program Director and other faculty for the design and implementation of the behavioral health curriculum, ensuring residents receive training sufficient to meet and exceed the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education Program Requirements for the residency program. Incumbent will focus on various domains including behavioral and community health, human behavior, psychiatry, ethics, doctor-patient communication, cultural humility, quality improvement, interdisciplinary approach, and well-being (for residents and faculty). Such training occurs during specialized didactic presentations, during rotations, one-on-one or group sessions with residents, and longitudinally while co-precepting with faculty physicians. The Behavioral Health Specialist/Educator will engage in scholarly activities within the Family Medicine Residency Program. Minimum Qualifications Required Education: PhD or equivalent Other Education if applicable: PhD or PsyD in Clinical Psychology from an APA-accredited institution and successful completion of an APA-accredited residency program Certifications or Licenses Required: Licensed to practice clinical psychology in Louisiana or valid LCSW license in Louisiana; credentialed with all required entities before hire Substitution: Master’s degree in social work and successful completion of accredited clinical internship Preferred Qualifications Preferred Experience: Experience in population health, quality improvement, and statistical analysis is a plus Additional Information About Our School/Department Comprehensive benefits are available to eligible employees and their dependents including health, life, dental, and vision insurance; flexible spending accounts; retirement plans; generous annual and sick leave, and14 paid holidays per year. See following link for more details on our benefits offerings: LSUHSC, New Orleans - Benefits Other employee benefits include a full-service credit union, wellness benefits featuring complimentary fitness center membership for employees and their spouses, employee assistance program, campus assistance program, and pet insurance option. More information about these benefits can be found on this webpage: Additional Benefits

jobs.title: Instructor of Radiologic Technology
jobs.description: Instructor of Radiologic Technology Reports to:Provost and Vice-President for Academic Affairs, Dean of Academic Affairs, and Chair of the Department of Health Sciences; Directly to Radiologic Technology Program Director Supervises:Radiologic Technology Students Basic Function:Provides didactic, clinical/laboratory instruction and clinical supervision to current students. Provides evaluation of and advisement to current students. Participates in periodic review and development of the program. Qualifications:Position requires a bachelor’s degree; a master’s degree is preferred. Must possess current, unrestricted certification with the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists and licensure from the Louisiana State Radiologic Technology Board of Examiners. Two years of full-time professional experience as a radiographer is required. Major Duties: Foster the Mission of the University in teaching, research and service. Conduct oneself in a professional and respectful manner. Prepare and plan lecture and clinical/laboratory instruction in the assigned Radiologic Technology program courses in accordance with course curriculum and learning outcomes. Prepare and/or maintain current course syllabi for courses taught. Prepare and correct student examinations and work assignments. Evaluate student performance in lecture and clinical/laboratory courses. Facilitate student clinical learning at clinical sites in accordance with accreditation requirements. Work with clinical preceptors and/or managers at clinical sites to create equitable learning opportunities for students, ensure clinical staff is knowledgeable of proper student supervision and competency testing rules and foster a positive learning environment for all. Clinical teaching and supervision workload require duties of a radiologic technologist. Travel to educational facilities is required. Meet all regularly scheduled classes. Post and keep at least six regular office hours (Adjunct faculty should be available to students outside of class at mutually convenient times.). Provide student academic advisement. Schedule student conferences to review individual student progress. Submit grades according to prescribed guidelines. Handle student documentation, evaluation and attendance records. Support Program Director in evaluation and revision of program curriculum, learning outcomes and program assessment. Assist in student recruitment, applicant and community activities. Attend University-wide and departmental meetings and commencement exercises. Perform any other related duties as assigned. Equal OpportunityThe University of Holy Cross assures equal opportunity for all qualified persons without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, handicap, marital status, or veterans’ status in the admission to, participation in, or employment of its programs and activities.Applicants who meet the qualifications listed above are invited to submit a complete application packet, consisting of a cover letter, resume, transcripts, and three letters of recommendation to Shavondra Wallace, HR@uhcno.edu in a single submission. Incomplete application packets will not be considered. Navigation

jobs.description: T hank you for your interest in employment with Louisiana Tech University. Louisiana Tech University invites applications for a 10-month, full-time position as Director of the Early Childhood Education Center (ECEC) and Instructor in the Human Development and Family Science (HDFS) program. The Early Childhood Education Center is a high-quality early learning environment serving children ages 3 and 4 and functions as a laboratory school that supports both child development and university instruction. The ECEC provides a model setting for developmentally appropriate practice, observation, and applied learning for undergraduate students through structured observations, practicum placements, and student employment opportunities. The Director provides vision, leadership, and daily oversight of the ECEC while advancing its role as a premier early childhood education center and an integral component of the HDFS curriculum. The position also includes teaching responsibilities within the Human Development and Family Science program, contributing to student learning, mentoring, and program development. The Director reports to the Director of the School of Human Ecology. Responsibilities include: Provide leadership and administration of the Early Childhood Education Center, including supervision of lead teachers and staff, program planning, and compliance with state licensing and quality standards. Maintain and enhance the ECEC’s role as a model early childhood program and laboratory school supporting student learning and engagement. Facilitate high-impact learning experiences for university students through observations, practicum placements, and student employment. Teach three undergraduate courses in Human Development and Family Science per academic year. Support recruitment, retention, and success of HDFS students. Collaborate with faculty to integrate the ECEC into academic programming and experiential learning opportunities. Engage with families, community partners, and university stakeholders to promote program excellence and visibility. Qualifications: Master’s degree in Human Development and Family Science, Early Childhood Education, Child Development or a closely related field required. Demonstrated experience in early childhood program administration or leadership. Experience teaching or mentoring college students preferred. Strong commitment to developmentally appropriate practice and experiential learning. Effective communication and organizational skills. We seek a candidate with a strong commitment to high-quality research as well as undergraduate and graduate education and expertise in Coastal/Marine Sciences or Coastal Engineering with specialization in fluvial, coastal or deltaic sedimentology, hydrology and sediment transport or surface hydrology/hydraulics. Candidates must hold a Ph.D. in Geoscience, Marine Science, Civil Engineering, Coastal Engineering or a related field, must be academically qualified to teach, and must meet all other position requirements at the time of selection including research experience in coastal Louisiana. The position involves teaching courses in the areas of fluvial geomorphology and river dynamics, coastal/marine sedimentology and stratigraphy, sediment transport, surface hydrology, and environmental engineering, and contributing to the department’s core curricula in coastal and environmental science and civil and environmental engineering. Job Posting Title: Online Program Instructor - Industrial Engineering Position Type: Faculty Department: LSUAM Engineering - School of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (Dimitris E Nikitopoulos (00006339)) Work Location: 3261 Patrick F. Taylor Hall Pay Grade: Academic Job Description: Louisiana State University (LSU) in Baton Rouge invites applications and nominations for a part-time Online Program Instructor of Industrial Engineering in the Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MIE). LSU is the Flagship University of the State of Louisiana, with its main campus located in the vibrant city of Baton Rouge, offering many cultural and recreational opportunities and high-quality affordable housing. The MIE Department is the largest one in the College of Engineering with B.S., M.S. and Ph.D. degree programs in both Mechanical Engineering and Industrial Engineering. Appointment will be made at the Instructor level, though applicants with exceptional qualifications and experience may be considered at higher Instructor ranks. Job Summary: Contribute to the educational mission of the Department and support the LSU Online initiative by delivering high-quality online instruction in the graduate Industrial Engineering program. Responsibilities include teaching graduate-level Industrial Engineering lecture and laboratory courses in accordance with LSU Online standards and best practices for online learning. Job Description: 90% Teach graduate-level Industrial Engineering courses in online formats in accordance with LSU Online standards and best practices. Develop and maintain course materials, assignments, assessments, and instructional content using the university’s learning management system. Assess student performance and submit grades in accordance with university policies and academic deadlines. 10% Facilitate student learning and engagement through effective online communication, virtual office hours, and timely feedback on assignments and assessments. Collaborate with faculty and IE program leadership to support curriculum development, continuous improvement, and accreditation efforts. Minimum Qualifications: Ph.D. in an engineering discipline. Experience in Industrial Engineering areas such as systems engineering, supply chain and logistics, ergonomics, analytics, operations research, and related disciplines. Preferred Qualifications: Ph.D. in an engineering discipline; 10 years of experience or more. Specific Experience: The ideal candidate will have significant professional experience in Industrial Engineering areas such as systems engineering, supply chain and logistics, ergonomics, analytics, operations research, and related disciplines. The online instructor will bring extensive industry experience and current applications of Industrial Engineering practices into the virtual classroom, integrating real-world examples, emerging technologies, and applied problem-solving approaches to enhance graduate-level online instruction. Preferred Certifications: A bachelors degree and/or certificates in industrial and/or systems and/or aerospace and/or nuclear and/or mechanical engineering. Additional Job Description: Special Instructions: Please attach as one single PDF to your online application: cover letter, comprehensive curriculum vitae, teaching statement and three professional references including name, title, phone number and e-mail address. A copy of your transcript(s) may be attached to your application (if available). However, original transcripts are required prior to hire. Job Posting Title: Postdoctoral Scholar Position Type: Other Academic Department: LSUAM Engineering - CM - Contracts (Hessam AzariJafari (00341709)) Work Location: 3319 Patrick F. Taylor Hall Pay Grade: Other Academic Job Description: Job Summary: This position is an entry level position to perform research and quantify the market potential for solid carbon from turquoise hydrogen in construction materials. The work includes developing a material flow analysis framework for solid carbon update in the U.S. asphalt and concrete markets, analyzing how solid carbon incorporation affects the mechanical, thermal, and durability performance of these materials, mapping performance thresholds such as strength, modulus, and fatigue against incorporation rates to define safe and effective use limits, designing pavement and building elements to quantify material savings from the single element up to the community and network scale, developing regional building and infrastructure archetypes, estimating solid carbon demand by material type and region, and preparing technical reports and journal manuscripts. The role also involves coordinating project data and analyses and presenting results to the stakeholders.. A Ph.D. in civil, structural, or materials engineering or a closely related field is required. Job Responsibilities: 80%: Conducts experiments and performs research under the close supervision of an Assistant Professor. 15%: Coordinating project data and analysis with the research team and presenting results to stakeholders. 5%: Ongoing training and professional development Minimum Qualifications: Education Level: Ph.D. Specific Degree: Terminal degree and related coursework in civil, structural, materials engineering or a closely related field Specific Experience: Material flow analysis and materials performance. Additional Job Description: Special Instructions: For questions or concerns regarding the status of your application, salary ranges, or other details pertaining to the position, please contact Dr. AzariJarfari at Hessam.AzariJafari@lsu.edu.
